# DocCode 0.4.0

DocCode is a local desktop application that generates interactive HTML documentation from source code using a local LLM via Ollama.

0.4.0 is the first release since 0.2.0 and includes the changes originally prepared for 0.3.0. It adds a live generation progress screen, replaces the hand-written Markdown renderer, simplifies the vector-index build, and ships Linux packages alongside the Windows installer.

## What's new

- **Live generation progress.** A dedicated progress screen now shows the full pipeline (`Scan → Index → Plan → Generate → Finalize`), a stage progress bar, live counters for scanned files, indexed chunks and documented components, and an elapsed timer. Progress is driven by real pipeline counters; stages without unit counts show phase status instead of time-based estimates.
- **New Markdown renderer.** Generated documentation is rendered through `pulldown-cmark` with CommonMark and table support. Raw HTML from the model is escaped, and links with unsafe schemes (for example `javascript:`) are displayed as text instead of becoming clickable links.
- **Linux packages are included.** The release now contains a `.deb` package and an AppImage in addition to the Windows installer.
- **Build fix.** `packaging\build-release.ps1` now passes `-Version` correctly when building the Windows installer.

### Under the hood

- The in-memory vector store and the `qdrant` Cargo feature were removed. Qdrant Edge is now the only vector backend, so the `--no-default-features` build mode is gone.
- The unused `AiClient` trait, `async-trait` dependency, example binaries, duplicate wrappers, ETA estimators, and other dead plumbing were removed. The codebase and test surface are noticeably smaller.
- README build and test instructions were simplified to match the single supported configuration.

## Code signing

Windows builds produced by the tag-triggered `Release` workflow are signed with Authenticode (SHA-256 + RFC 3161 timestamp). `doccode.exe` and the installer show **SignPath Foundation** as the publisher instead of “Unknown publisher.” Linux packages are not signed.

Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org).

For details on what is signed, how requests are approved, and how to verify downloads, see [CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md](https://github.com/ksen145/DocCode/blob/main/CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md).

```powershell
Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\DocCode-0.4.0-x64-setup.exe |
  Format-List Status, SignerCertificate, TimeStamperCertificate
```

`Status` should be `Valid`, and the publisher should be **SignPath Foundation**. Compare the SHA-256 hash with `SHA256SUMS.txt` from the same release.

The signature confirms authorship and file integrity, but it does not replace reputation: SmartScreen may warn on the first downloads of a new signature. This warning goes away as the release is downloaded more widely.

## Linux packages

Install the Debian/Ubuntu package:

```bash
sudo dpkg -i doccode_0.4.0_amd64.deb
```

Or run the portable AppImage:

```bash
chmod +x DocCode-0.4.0-x86_64.AppImage
./DocCode-0.4.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

The packages are built in an Ubuntu 22.04 container (glibc 2.35+) and verified for package contents, desktop entry, AppStream metadata, and runtime dependencies.

## Documentation and license

- README is available in English (default) and Russian (`README.ru.md`).
- The project is licensed under MIT — see `LICENSE`.
- Code signing policy: `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md`.

## Requirements

A running Ollama instance and the following models:

```bash
ollama pull gemma4:e4b        # documentation generation
ollama pull nomic-embed-text  # embeddings for the vector index
ollama pull d1                # quality control (optional)
```

If the D1 model is not available, disable the check in settings — the documentation will be marked as unverified.

## Upgrading from 0.2.0

The installer can be installed over the previous version; no uninstall is required. Settings in `%APPDATA%\doccode` are preserved. No configuration migration is needed.

## Known limitations

- Only Ollama is supported; other OpenAI-compatible backends are not connected yet.
- Embeddings are computed sequentially — indexing large projects takes noticeable time.
- There is no incremental index update: the index is rebuilt from scratch.
- D1 is a conservative filter: `needs_review` means manual review is required, not that generation failed.
- The generated site shell is currently localized in Russian; the selected language affects the documentation language.
- Linux packages are unsigned.
- macOS has not been tested separately.
